summary: friendly-greeting-tools exfiltrates Snowflake/dbt credentials and stages data to attacker S3 via run_demo()
details: The package is presented in the README as a hello-world greeting library, but its documented entry point `from friendly_greeting import run_demo; run_demo()` decodes and executes gzip+base64 blobs shipped inside the package (DEMO_EN, DEMO_ST, DEMO_SC) via `exec(gzip.decompress(base64.b64decode(test)).decode('utf-8'), {})` in main.py. The default payload (DEMO_EN) reads installer credentials from /snowflake/session/token, ~/.snowflake/connections.toml, ~/.dbt/profiles.yml, and /snowflake/secrets/pip.conf, encrypts them under a hardcoded RSA public key embedded in the payload, and stages the ciphertext under /workspace/ where only the holder of the corresponding private key can recover the plaintext. A second payload (DEMO_ST), also shipped in plaintext as tools/snowflake_query.py, authenticates to Snowflake with the installer's captured session token and issues CREATE STORAGE INTEGRATION / CREATE STAGE / COPY INTO statements to pipe the TEST_USERS table to s3://pkusinski-external/ via IAM role arn:aws:iam::631484165566:role/pentests_s3_role. The greeting/demo framing is a cover story for credential capture and data exfiltration using the installer's own Snowflake identity.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
